text:
Bobby McMann scored 29 goals last season, mostly in Toronto, and the Kraken traded for that player. So far they have a different one: pointless in six, one point in his last ten games, and Seattle has 42% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice.

Our numbers call the slump mixed. He's getting a few fewer chances than usual, and the ones he gets aren't going in (6.7% shooting against a typical 13). The first part is the worry. He's on a line with Jordan Eberle and Chandler Stephenson that has been out-chanced badly (39% of the expected goals), and that's not a situation that fixes itself.

He's a transition player, with more than half his shots off the rush in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, on a team that hasn't had the puck much. An undrafted free agent who made himself a scorer, he has earned patience. Our range still says 19 to 34 goals.
